title: Rational and $\Qlb$ purity
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated morphism of pure relative dimension $d$
between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $K$ lie in the $E$-coefficient
category of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], respectively the
$\Qlb$-coefficient category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], presented
by a normalized integral system (a lattice) as in
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Then

$$
\gamma_{f,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$

is an isomorphism in the corresponding category: rationalization along
[prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] and finite extension of coefficient
fields carry the adic purity isomorphism of
[thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] to the $E$- and $\Qlb$-purity
isomorphisms.

proof.text: Step 1 (rationalization on objects and morphisms). By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], an $E$-object is an integral object $K$ with its Hom modules localized; write $Q_E$ for this rationalization functor and, as in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], put $H_E=Lf_E^*(-)(d)[2d]$ and $G_E=Rf_E^!$. The schemes $X,Y$ are noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to their structure morphisms over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$), and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. On these schemes, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies the integral category used by this rationalization with [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Its lattices are therefore in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]: if the first reduction has cohomology in $[r,s]$, every reduction has Tor amplitude in that same interval. The hypotheses of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] now hold, including separated finite-type source and target, pure dimension $d\geq0$, completed coefficients and uniform finite Tor amplitude; it gives an integral isomorphism with the prescribed finite reductions. It asserts no uniqueness or naturality of arbitrary coherent lifts. Choose simultaneously the compatible realizations $\gamma_{E,K}$ supplied by [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]; these have those same prescribed reductions and form an integral linear natural transformation between the exact linear operation functors. All subsequent uses of $\gamma_{E,K}$ refer to this compatible choice. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to this transformation and the two operation functors. By [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], the rational exceptional functor is defined by rationalization of the compatible integral functor; this is exactly the functor just extended. The rational pullback and tensor definitions in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], together with [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], identify $Q_EH_EK$ with $Lf_E^*(Q_EK)(d)[2d]$. Set $\gamma_{E,Q_EK}=Q_E(\gamma_{E,K})$. Its inverse is $Q_E(\gamma_{E,K}^{-1})$, since applying a functor to the two inverse equations gives both inverse equations after rationalization. For a localized morphism $u/\varpi_E^r$, integral naturality for $u$ gives $G_E(u)\gamma_{E,K}=\gamma_{E,L}H_E(u)$; multiply by $\varpi_E^{-r}$ to obtain naturality for that localized morphism. Thus a rational isomorphism between any two lattice presentations intertwines their purity maps, proving independence of presentation.

source.place: Proof, Step 1 (E-stage): rationalization of a lattice; explicit naturality and inverse equations supplied by this repair

proof.text:
Step 2 (finite extensions and their equations). For $E\subset F$, let $T_{F/E}$ be [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The helper's integral $C_{F/E,W}$ is ordinary tensor by the completed coefficient sheaf, as is the integral functor underlying this $T$. The natural isomorphism $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies it with the strict inverse-limit scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]; its hypothesis holds because the lattices are derived complete. Thus there is no identification of these two constructions by definition alone. Work in the helper's ordinary-tensor presentation, whose associator is precisely the tensor associator specified in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. For the simultaneously chosen integral family of Step 1, rationalize the natural comparison equation of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. Since $T_{F/E}=Q_FC_{F/E}$ on integral representatives, this gives, on every object,
$$b_{F/E,K}\,T_{F/E,X}(\gamma_{E,K})=\gamma_{F,T_{F/E,Y}K}\,a_{F/E,K}.$$
For the coefficient-passage exceptional functor defined in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], use the rationalized integral $b$ as its scalar comparison. The helper identifies that integral map with the adjunction mate and proves its coherence, so no independent Verdier-duality comparison is needed. The twist comparison is the coefficient comparison of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The identity and composition equations in the integral helper remain equations after applying rationalization; the helper also gives shift compatibility of both exact comparisons. Hence the displayed equation respects the unit, shifts and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Solving it for inverses gives
$$T_{F/E,X}(\gamma_{E,K}^{-1})\,b_{F/E,K}^{-1}=a_{F/E,K}^{-1}\,\gamma_{F,T_{F/E,Y}K}^{-1}.$$
Thus both the purity family and its inverse satisfy the finite-stage compatibility required for descent.

source.place: Proof, Step 2 (Qbar-stage): compatibility of finite coefficient extensions, made explicit before common-stage descent

proof.text:
Step 3 (common-stage descent). In [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], an object is a pair $(E,K)$ and a morphism to $(F,L)$ has a representative $u:T_{M/E}K\to T_{M/F}L$ over a common finite extension $M$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] to the two scalar-compatible functor families $H_E$ and $G_E$ and to the compatible transformations of Step 2. Explicitly, the purity component at $(E,K)$ is represented by $\gamma_{E,K}$ and its inverse by $\gamma_{E,K}^{-1}$. For the representative $u$, naturality at $M$ is
$$G_M(u)\,\gamma_{M,T_{M/E}K}=\gamma_{M,T_{M/F}L}\,H_M(u).$$
Put $U=T_{M/E}K$ and $V=T_{M/F}L$, and abbreviate comparison components at $K,L$ by subscripts $E,F$. By the representative formula of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], the two functor images are represented by $a_F^{-1}H_M(u)a_E$ and $b_F^{-1}G_M(u)b_E$. Step 2 and the displayed naturality equation give
$$\begin{aligned}
(b_F^{-1}G_M(u)b_E)T_{M/E,X}(\gamma_{E,K})
&=b_F^{-1}G_M(u)\gamma_{M,U}a_E\\
&=b_F^{-1}\gamma_{M,V}H_M(u)a_E\\
&=T_{M/F,X}(\gamma_{F,L})(a_F^{-1}H_M(u)a_E).
\end{aligned}$$
This is the required naturality on $[M,u]$. For a larger stage $N\supset M$, denote the scalar associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] by $A^W_{N,M,E}:T_{N/M,W}T_{M/E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{N/E,W}$. The transported representative is
$$u_N=A^Y_{N,M,F}\,T_{N/M,Y}(u)\,(A^Y_{N,M,E})^{-1}.$$
For $a$ the composition equation from Step 2 is
$$a_{N/E,K}A^X_{N,M,E,H_EK}=H_N(A^Y_{N,M,E,K})\,a_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}\,T_{N/M,X}(a_{M/E,K}),$$
and the equation for $b$ replaces $a,H$ by $b,G$. Apply $T_{N/M,X}$ to the three-line naturality calculation above and substitute these two composition equations, first at $K$ and then at $L$. Naturality of $a_{N/M}$ and $b_{N/M}$ moves $T_{N/M}(H_M(u))$ and $T_{N/M}(G_M(u))$ through those comparisons; the purity square of Step 2 moves the two transported purity components through them. The adjacent inverse comparisons cancel. Conjugating the source and target by $A^X_{N,M,E}$ and $A^X_{N,M,F}$ leaves exactly the displayed calculation at $N$ with $u_N$. Thus enlargement gives the same morphism class and the same naturality equation. Equality of two representative classes is equality after such a common enlargement by [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], so the calculation respects that equivalence relation. The two composite maps of the descended purity and inverse are represented by $\gamma_{E,K}^{-1}\gamma_{E,K}=1$ and $\gamma_{E,K}\gamma_{E,K}^{-1}=1$, so both composites are identities. These are the claimed $\Qlb$ purity isomorphisms, independent of the representative stage.

split_report.summary: Repair of the landing refusal for a changed cited statement. Re-read the current adic reconstruction statement and its normalized-DVR proof: it supplies existence and exact reductions, not uniqueness of a coherent lift. Update the verbatim citation and every use of that interface. The integral helper now asserts existence of a simultaneous natural, scalar-compatible family with those reductions, rather than naturality of arbitrary reconstructed lifts. Step 1 explicitly selects that family before localization and Steps 2--3 descend it. Replace the helper common-local-model tower reference by the normalized-DVR definition, and cite the actual integral compact-support construction. Recheck every item citation, all geometric and Tor hypotheses, sources, searches and small cases. No changes to the four target declarations, chapter, unit or live project. Independent second reading: distinguish strict inverse-limit integral scalar extension from ordinary tensor by completed coefficients, cite the existing finite-free comparison, and state the helper equations in the tensor presentation used by rational scalar extension. Fresh Mathlib searches and source/edge-case checks recorded in the second-reading report.
split_report.blueprint: Imported proof Step 1 is realized by Step 1; imported Step 2 is realized by Steps 2--3. New integral comparison helper supplies the compatibility missing from the original circular citation.

Generic comparison of strict inverse-limit integral scalar extension with tensor by the finite-free completed coefficient sheaf. It aligns the purity helper with the rational scalar-extension package; no purity-unit node supplies this construction comparison.
